doc.title: Ann Rabson interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, September 21, 2007

title: Relationships and a career in music
summary: She found a partner who is not jealous of her success, unlike earlier men who wanted her to stop playing.

story.theme_name: Meeting, marrying and raising a family
story.community_name: Meeting, courting and marrying: musicians' love lives

blocks.x: That’s great. Being a professional musician and the process of trying to be a professional musician, has that made relationships harder to keep?
Yeah. It absolutely has. I had to find somebody who — I don’t know if it was because of his being raised by women, strong women, or what, but I had to I’m going to cough again here

Yeah. I had to find somebody who was happy for me to be successful at something that he couldn’t do, and who doesn’t have a jealous bone in his body, or if he does he certainly has never showed it. It doesn’t seem to be in his repertoire. Not just sexual jealousy but any kind of jealousy. And all of the women that he’s always liked have all been very strong and very independent and so that worked out very well. But prior to that I had a lot of men who — and I know that male musicians have the same problem — men fall in love with me because I play music and then they want me to stop playing music.
I’ve got to write a song about that. But I know that happens to men too.
